$comment: FIGMA -> CANVAS parity map. Every identifier is real: tsx files exist in reference/figma-build/src/screens (or components/ui.tsx), canvas names exist in canvas-app/src. Verified by scripts/check_design_parity.py, narrated in docs/FIGMA_CANVAS_PARITY.md. Parity values: PASS | MINOR DRIFT | PLATFORM SUBSTITUTION | FAIL. FAIL blocks release.

screens.note: The Figma launch/dispatch screen is App.StartScreen evaluating MF_StartScreen in canvas. Power Apps renders its own loading state before StartScreen resolves; a hand-built splash screen would add a frame the platform already provides.

The kill switch (MaintenanceMode) blocks exactly as the Figma screen does. A schema-version mismatch deliberately does NOT block: users keep read access to their own status and MF_SchemaMismatchDetail renders on scrDiagnostics. Functional decision recorded in canvas-app/formulas/App.Formulas.fx.

One canvas screen covers both no-mapping and unresolved-scope; both states resolve to the same operator action (fix the MF Security Mapping row) and both offer the request-access route, exactly as the two Figma screens do.
Request access is a button here, never a navigation tab - matching the approved design.
Reached only from scrNoAccess, as in the Figma flow.
Primary action, not a tab: BASE_TABS is exactly Home / My Package / Calendar and colNavigation matches.
Queue and detail are one canvas screen (gallery plus detail pane) instead of two Figma screens. Same information, one fewer navigation hop; density preserved.
See ReviewQueue.tsx - the detail pane of the combined screen.
scrInstallations is the list level above it (the Installations tab); scrInstallation is the workspace itself.

Grant administration happens in the SharePoint list UI for MF Security Mapping, not in the canvas app. Power Apps Visible/Filter is not a security boundary (docs/security-open-issue.md, OPEN); an in-app grants editor would imply an authority the app does not have.
A reusable canvas component rather than a screen; instantiated wherever a list can be empty.

canvas_only_screens.note: Not in figma-build PM_TABS; the directive nav supersedes it.
Audit trail destination; not in figma-build PM_TABS.

canvas_only_screens.origin: reached from scrExceptions rows, never a tab
figma-build PM_TABS 'Installations' tab; the list level above InstallationWorkspace.tsx, which has no dedicated tsx of its own
the Admin tab's content (requirement catalogue administration)
canvas_only_screens.note: figma-build's admin tab shows platform health; the canvas Admin tab edits requirements and scrDiagnostics carries health.

components.note: 1px status border, radius 2, label+icon, never colour alone - all per spec. Chip is 32px tall against Figma's ~20px: minimum touch target wins over visual scale (accessibility > visual). Border colour follows the status text token rather than Figma's separate border tokens, which were designed against the pre-fix amber/yellow inks; docs/accessibility.md is the arbiter.

navigation.note: base_tabs equals figma-build BASE_TABS exactly. afsvc_tabs follows the directive's approved AFSVC experience (adds Exceptions and Activity to figma-build's PM_TABS). Nav badge-count chips from figma-build are omitted: MINOR DRIFT - a live count on every tab means N delegable count queries on every screen paint; the queue screens themselves carry the counts.

tokens.note: Canvas values are authoritative post-accessibility-fix values; figma values recorded where they differ. docs/accessibility.md holds the ratios.

clrStatusAmber.deviation: APPROVED - accessibility re-tint; the Figma CSS predates the amber/yellow separation fix (docs/accessibility.md)

clrStatusGray.deviation: APPROVED - minor darkening for contrast on the gray chip

clrFocus.deviation: Fluent focus ring; no Figma counterpart

typography.figma_design_font: Inter (design substitute only; @import removed from index.css intentionally)
typography.production_font: Segoe UI (Power Apps native; Segoe UI Variable on Windows 11+)
typography.note: No substitution needed: the production font the Figma package names is what Power Apps renders natively. Text ramp maps Body->Body1, Caption->Caption1, Subtitle->Subtitle1 in scripts/gen_msapp_source.py.

assets.runtime_fetches: none - no CDN, Google Fonts, Figma CDN, or Azure Blob dependency anywhere in the canvas source or msapp
assets.note: AFSVC-Shield.png in the Figma package is unused by the approved screens; nothing is embedded.
